walkthroughs.body_html:
Cells grow, copy DNA, then divide.

Stages: G1 grow, S phase (DNA copied), G2 grow more, then mitosis (PMAT) and cytokinesis. Two identical daughter cells.

Embryonic stem cells can form any cell type. Adult stem cells (e.g. bone marrow) form a limited range.

asks you to evaluate uses — treating diabetes, paralysis, blood disorders — vs ethical and rejection concerns.

Stimulus → receptor → sensory neurone → CNS → motor neurone → effector → response.

A reflex skips the brain — it goes through the spinal cord via a relay neurone for speed.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.

Stem cells are taken only from embryos and cannot be found in adults.
Stem cells are simply cells that haven't grown big enough yet.
An undifferentiated cell capable of dividing to produce more stem cells or differentiating into specialised cell types.

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.
Stem cells are simply cells that haven't grown big enough yet.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.

mcqs.q: A reflex arc lets you pull your hand from a hot object before you feel pain. Why is the response so fast?
options: The impulse takes a short route through the spinal cord, not the conscious brain.
Reflexes use hormones which act instantly.
The brain processes the decision faster than normal.
The impulse skips the relay neurone entirely.

mcqs.q: At a synapse, how does the signal pass from one neurone to the next?
options: A neurotransmitter chemical diffuses across the gap.
The electrical impulse jumps directly across the gap.
The two neurones fuse together.
A hormone is released into the blood.

mcqs.q: Stem cells from a patient could be used to grow replacement tissue. What property of stem cells makes this possible?
options: They can divide and differentiate into different cell types.
They are already fully specialised.
They cannot divide once formed.
They contain no DNA.
